# Prometheus Metric Naming

A single per-project pattern for naming Prometheus metrics in exporters,
plugins, and any service that publishes a `/metrics` endpoint.

## Pattern

```text
<prefix>_[<subsystem>_]<name>_<unit_or_role>
```

| Token            | Purpose                                                                                                                       |
|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `<prefix>`       | Exporter namespace. One per project. snake_case. Matches the package / repo name. Example: `claude_quota_`, `nina_`, `phd2_`. |
| `<subsystem>`    | Optional. Distinguishes major subsystems within an exporter that spans multiple hardware or feature classes. Example: `nina_mount_*`, `nina_camera_*`, `alpaca_camera_*`. Omit on single-domain exporters (`claude_quota_utilization`, not `claude_quota_quota_utilization`). |
| `<name>`         | Descriptive, snake_case.                                                                                                      |
| `<unit_or_role>` | Required when applicable. See suffix table below.                                                                             |

## Suffix table

| Suffix                 | When                                                                  |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `_total`               | Counter.                                                              |
| `_seconds`             | Duration. Also acceptable for absolute time when the name itself contains a timestamp word (`_at_seconds`, `_resets_at_seconds`, `_expires_at_seconds`). |
| `_timestamp_seconds`   | Absolute time (Unix epoch seconds) when the name does NOT already read as a timestamp. Example: `last_fetch_timestamp_seconds`. |
| `_bytes`               | Size.                                                                 |
| `_celsius`             | Temperature.                                                          |
| `_percent`             | Percentage 0..100. HELP must say "0..100".                            |
| `_ratio`               | Ratio 0..1. Optional; may omit if the HELP text states the range.     |
| `_degrees`             | Angular.                                                              |
| Other physical units   | Spell out: `_hpa`, `_mps`, `_mmh`, `_lux`, `_arcsec`, `_ms`, `_mpsas`. |

## Omit the unit suffix when

- The gauge is boolean (0 or 1). HELP text spells out "1 if X, else 0".
- The gauge value is an enum integer code. HELP text spells out the
  codes.
- The value is a dimensionless count that is not a Prometheus counter
  (use `_count` or no suffix).

## Always

- snake_case end-to-end. camelCase prefixes (e.g. `timeOfDay_`) are
  grandfathered for existing exporters but not used for new ones.
- HELP text is mandatory for every metric.
- Cardinality lives in labels, not name suffixes. Per-instance data
  (camera name, device id, bucket name) goes in a label.

## Never

- Embed token values, status codes, or other dynamic data in the
  metric name. Use labels.
- Use generic placeholders (`value`, `data`, `metric`, `field`) in
  the name body. The name itself should describe the thing measured.
- Repeat the prefix inside the name body
  (`claude_quota_quota_utilization`).

## Examples

```text
# claude-quota-exporter
claude_quota_utilization{bucket="five_hour"}                       # ratio 0..1, suffix omitted, range in HELP
claude_quota_resets_at_seconds{bucket="five_hour"}                  # absolute time; _seconds OK because name reads as timestamp
claude_quota_fetch_success_total                                    # counter
claude_quota_last_fetch_timestamp_seconds                           # absolute time; _timestamp_seconds because name does not read as timestamp
claude_quota_access_token_expires_at_seconds                        # absolute time, _seconds OK because of _at_
claude_quota_credentials_present                                    # 0/1, no suffix
claude_quota_refresh_failure_total                                  # counter

# nina-prometheus-exporter
nina_camera_temperature_celsius{camera="ASI2600"}                   # temperature
nina_weather_humidity_percent{site="primary"}                       # 0..100
nina_autofocus_failure_total{reason="..."}                          # counter

# phd2-exporter
phd2_rms{axis="ra"}                                                  # ratio-like, no suffix; HELP describes
phd2_connected{site="primary"}                                       # 0/1
```

## When a name violates the standard

- New exporter: pick the compliant name.
- Existing exporter, no consumers yet: rename freely.
- Existing exporter, consumers in place: keep the old name, add a
  parallel compliant name, deprecate the old one in HELP text.
  Remove on the next major version.

## Rationale

- The prefix-per-exporter rule means `prometheus.io/scrape`-style
  discovery and a single recording rule can match an exporter's
  output by name pattern alone.
- The unit suffix lets PromQL writers reason about a metric without
  reading HELP. `nina_weather_temperature_celsius` is unambiguous;
  `nina_weather_temperature` is not.
- The `_total` suffix on counters is part of the Prometheus on-the-wire
  format (the OpenMetrics standard documents it as the canonical
  counter suffix). prometheus_client appends it for you in some bindings
  but not all; spell it out so the wire form is consistent regardless of
  binding.
- `_timestamp_seconds` over `_seconds` for absolute time avoids the
  ambiguity that `_seconds` can mean either "duration" or "epoch
  seconds". The reader has to know which one applies. Where the metric
  name itself says it's a timestamp (`_at_seconds`, `_expires_at_seconds`),
  the redundancy is unnecessary.
